title: Southern Blot Protocol
author: Oriol Busquets
materials: While one southern blot probe can be sufficient to determine the genomic integrity of a genome edited locus, we usually recommend a 3’ and 5’ probe in combination with suitable restriction digests to fully evaluate a genome edited genomic locus. It is advisable to establish robust enzyme digestion and probe functionality on control gDNA before running experiments. We usually design primers for PCRs with an annealing temperature at 58 C. However, in case of problems to obtain a clean PCR product, the best annealing temperature should be determined specifically for each primer set. To generate southern blot probes use AccuPrime‱ Taq DNA Polymerase, high fidelity; ThermoFisher.12346086 on WIBR3 (parental; RRID:CVCL_9767) gDNA using primers described above.
Thermocycler settings: (94 C - 2min) + 30 cycles (94 C - 30 sec + 58 C - 30 sec + 68 C - 1 min/kb) + (68 C - 10 min) + (16 C - ∞).

This method to obtain gDNA has been used on human embryonic stem cells on feeder and feeder free conditions and produces samples of sufficient quality for southern blot analyses. It may need to be adjusted/replaced in cases that higher quality gDNA is necessary or other cell types/frozen cell pellets are being used (example: DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kits (69504 QIAGEN). Remove media from hESC cultures and add Lysis buffer (1 ml/well in 6 well plate and 0.5 ml/well in 12 well plate) and incubate for several hours to Overnight at 37 °C .

steps.title: Prepare PCR Probe
steps.instruction: Generate and purify the DNA probe via PCR.

substeps.instruction: Prepare PCR reaction with 100-200 ng gDNA template, 1 µl sense primer (10 µM), 1 µl anti-sense primer (10 µM), 5 µl AccuPrime Buffer II, 0.2 µl AccuPrime Taq DNA Polymerase High Fidelity (1U), and molecular grade water to 50 µl.
Confirm probe purity by running a sample or the entire product on a 0.8% agarose gel.
Purify the gel band or remaining PCR product using the E.Z.N.A. Gel Extraction Kit (Omega Bio-Tek; D5000) following manufacturer instructions.

steps.title: Extract Genomic DNA
steps.instruction: Isolate gDNA from lysate using isopropanol precipitation.

substeps.instruction: Transfer up to 750 µL of lysate (Tris-Cl pH 8.5 100mM, EDTA 5mM, NaCl 200 mM, SDS 0.2%, proteinase K 100 µg/ml) into a 1.5ml Eppendorf tube.
Add an equal volume of isopropanol and shake vigorously (do not vortex) until a white filamentous pellet is observed.
Centrifuge at max speed (≥ 13000 x g) for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Decant/aspirate supernatant and add 1 mL of 70% ETOH.
Briefly shake (do not vortex) to wash the pellet.
Centrifuge again at max speed (≥ 13000 x g) for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Decant supernatant and aspirate residual liquid.
Air dry with the cap open for 10-20 minutes until the pellet becomes translucent; do not overdry.

steps.title: Resuspend and Digest gDNA
steps.instruction: Solubilize the DNA pellet and perform restriction digestion.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in TE buffer and solubilize for 12-24 hours at 56 °C.
Assemble restriction digest: 10-15 µg gDNA, Restriction Enzyme (4 U per 1 µg DNA, max 5 µl enzyme/reaction), 5 µl Buffer (e.g., rCutSmart), and molecular grade water to 50 µl.
Incubate samples at 37 °C for 6 hours to overnight (adjust temperature based on enzyme requirements).

steps.title: Electrophoresis and Gel Preparation
steps.instruction: Separate digested DNA and prepare the gel for transfer.

substeps.instruction: Run digested gDNA on a 0.8% agarose gel with ethidium bromide using low voltage.
Include a 1 kB ladder (1/5-1/10 dilution may be necessary) to discern molecular weight.
Image the gel with a UV reader to locate sample tracks and marker distribution.
Trim the areas of the gel above the wells with a razor blade, marking edges to maintain orientation.

steps.title: Depurination and Denaturation
steps.instruction: Treat the gel to increase DNA transfer efficiency.

substeps.instruction: Incubate gel in depurination buffer (0.25M HCl) for 15 minutes with gentle shaking.
Incubate gel in denaturation buffer (0.5M NaOH, 1.5M NaCl) for 45 minutes to 1 hour.

steps.title: Assemble DNA Transfer Structure
steps.instruction: Set up the osmotic transfer assembly to move DNA from gel to membrane.

substeps.instruction: Place a glass plate in a sideways position on a buffer reservoir tray.
Place Whatman paper sheets soaked in denaturation buffer on the glass, ensuring an overhang into the reservoir.
Place the gel on the paper in an inverted position (wells facing down).
Place a pre-wetted (denaturation buffer) nylon membrane (Amersham Hybond XL) on the gel, using a serological pipette as a roller to remove bubbles.
Place several pre-wetted (denaturation buffer) Whatman paper sheets on the membrane, removing bubbles with a pipette.
Apply parafilm strips around the edges of the gel to prevent buffer shortcuts.
Place a stack of dry paper towels on top and weight down with a tray and mild pressure.
Fill the reservoir with denaturation buffer and allow transfer for 6 hours to overnight.
Disassemble the structure, mark membrane orientation with pencil, and wash 3 times for 10 minutes each with 2xSSC buffer (0.3M NaCl, 0.03M sodium citrate).
Preheat two tubes containing 20 mL of Church buffer (1 mM EDTA, 0.5M NaPO4 pH 7.2, 7% SDS, 1% w/v BSA added fresh) to 62 °C - 65 °C.
Place the membrane in a cylinder (DNA side facing inwards) with 20 mL of preheated Church buffer.
Incubate in a hybridization chamber for at least 1 hour at 62 °C - 65 °C with constant rotation.

steps.title: Probe Labeling and Hybridization
steps.instruction: Label the DNA probe and hybridize it to the membrane.

substeps.instruction: Prepare radiolabeled probes (50 ng DNA/probe) using Prime-It II Random Primer Labeling Kit (300385-52; Agilent) and dCTP, [α-32P]-3000Ci/mmol 10mCi/ml EasyTide (BLU513H100UC) per vendor instructions.
Purify the probe using a resin-based column (Ilustra ProbeQuant G-50 Micro Columns) and add it to the second tube of preheated Church buffer.
Replace the blocking solution in the cylinder with the probe solution.
Incubate overnight at 62 °C - 65 °C with constant rotation.

steps.title: Stringency Washes
steps.instruction: Remove non-specific probe binding using SSC buffers.

substeps.instruction: Wash membranes using SSC buffers ranging from 2X (low stringency) to 0.2X (high stringency), all containing 0.2% SDS.
Perform each wash for 5-10 minutes at 62 °C - 65 °C under constant rotation/shaking (either in the chamber or a sealed container).
Use a Geiger counter between washes to track radioactivity; repeat and increase stringency until the signal is modest.

steps.title: Exposure and Detection
steps.instruction: Expose the membrane to film to visualize the DNA bands.

substeps.instruction: Seal membranes in plastic foil to prevent drying.
Place in a cassette and expose to Carestream Biomax MS Films for 24 to 72 hours at -80 °C.
Perform all manipulations before development in a dark room.
Develop the film using a film developing system.
